title: fix(vsharp): raise default deconvolution threshold 0.05 → 0.2 (robustness to noisy fields)
body:
## Summary
Raise the V-SHARP default deconvolution `threshold` from `0.05` to `0.2`.

The TSVD threshold drops the ill-conditioned low-frequency band where `|1 - S| < threshold`. On a clean field it is inert (0.05 and 0.2 give identical output), but on a noisy *estimated* field the low threshold tries to recover that band and amplifies field-mapping error. Every real pipeline feeds V-SHARP an estimated (not ground-truth) field, so 0.05 optimises for a case that doesn't occur in practice; 0.2 is more robust and sits on the plateau of that benefit.

Sanity-checked on the QSM Challenge 2.0 phantom (ROMEO field mapping → V-SHARP → dipole): 0.2 lowers composed NRMSE on every dipole tested, with no change on a clean field.

## Risk
- Clean/ground-truth field: unchanged (threshold inert there).
- No test asserts the default; `cargo check` clean; callers passing an explicit `threshold` are unaffected.

title: feat: overlap-tiled deep-learning inference + Hugging Face weight hosting
body:
## Summary

Two related changes that unblock running the deep-learning QSM models in memory-constrained targets (the in-browser WASM build) and fix cross-origin weight fetching:

### 1. Overlap-tiled DL inference (opt-in; default whole-volume)
Runs the deep-learning inversions patch-by-patch so peak memory is bounded by one patch instead of the whole volume (the 32-bit WASM heap overflows on clinical-size data).

- **`tiled.rs`**: `TileConfig{core,halo}`; `tiled_scatter` (shared driver — skips all-background tiles = free bounding box, runs parallel batches, masked scatter, progress); `tiled_field_inversion` (fully-convolutional field→χ nets); `tiled_volume_algorithm` (whole-algorithm tiling for the FFT-unrolled nets).
- **`OnnxModel::plan_for` / `OnnxPlan`**: compile the graph once and reuse across patches instead of re-optimizing on every `run` call.
- **`*_tiled` variants**: `xqsm`, `qsmnet(+)`, `ir2qsm` (sound, field→χ); `lpcnn`, `modl_qsm`, `nextqsm` (whole-algorithm — off-design/approximate, since their k-space step is global).
- **Pipeline**: `InversionConfig.tile: Option<(core,halo)>`; `run_dipole_inversion` dispatches DL algorithms to the tiled variant when set. Tiled progress bound relaxed `Fn`→`FnMut` so the pipeline's `&mut dyn FnMut` callback threads through.
- **example `xqsm_tiled_check`**: whole-volume vs tiled correlation / NRMSE benchmark.

Quality: tiling approximates the whole-volume network (r≈0.94 on 3 T data) — a patch can't see distant susceptibility sources; the halo trades memory for boundary accuracy.

### 2. Hugging Face weight hosting (CORS)
Swaps the registry weight URLs from OSF to the CORS-enabled HF model repo [`qsmxt/qsm-onnx-weights`](https://huggingface.co/qsmxt/qsm-onnx-weights) (`resolve/main`). Identical files (sha256/bytes unchanged). OSF sends no `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`, so the browser build can't fetch from it; HF serves `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`.

## Testing
- Builds clean with `onnx,parallel`, default, and `--no-default-features`.
- Native download from HF verified end-to-end (ureq follows the resolve→CDN redirect; downloaded file sha256 matches the registry).
- Tiled vs whole-volume validated on real 3 T data (r≈0.94).

## Release chain
First of three coordinated changes: **QSM.rs (this)** → QSMxT (repin + expose `--tile-size`/`--tile-halo` in CLI/TUI, qsmxt-config emits them) → qsmbly (repin, browser tiling defaults). OSF weights stay until this ships and is adopted.

title: feat: deep-learning QSM inference via ONNX (15 models)
body:
Adds native deep-learning QSM to QSM.rs: a queryable model **registry**, runtime **weight download + SHA-256-verified cache**, and pure-Rust **ONNX inference via tract**. Inference is byte-based, so the same code path runs natively (from the cache) and in **WASM** (bytes fetched by JS, handed back in). Weights are **never bundled** — they resolve from `$QSM_MODEL_DIR` / cache, or download on first use.

## Models

All parity-verified against the original framework and hosted on OSF (project `erv6n`):

| Model | Stage | parity vs reference |
|---|---|---|
| BFRnet | background removal | corr 1.000000 |
| xQSM, QSMnet, QSMnet+, AutoQSM, iQSM, iQSM+ | dipole inversion | corr 1.000000 |
| SUSEP-Net | χ-separation | corr 1.000000 |
| **NeXtQSM** | bfr + dipole (total field → χ) | corr 0.999980 vs genuine TF `nextqsm` |

Legacy TensorFlow nets (QSMnet(+), AutoQSM) are **clean-rebuilt in PyTorch** and re-exported to NCDHW ONNX, since tract can't run tf2onnx graphs. Full per-model conversion provenance (export scripts, weight dumps, reference generators) lives in `qsmci/scripts/onnx-export/`.

## NeXtQSM (the hard one)

A hybrid reimplementation, not a single forward net: a BFR U-Net followed by a **6-step variational dipole inversion** whose update backprops through a second U-Net. Two ONNX files (BFR forward + the VarNet regularizer gradient **hand-coded as a forward graph**), with the FFT data-consistency gradient and the unroll in Rust.

Its full-resolution conv adjoints are emitted as regular `Conv` ops (flipped + channel-swapped kernels) rather than `ConvTranspose` — otherwise both tract and ONNX Runtime allocate a **43.5 GB** col2im buffer and OOM. With that rewrite it reconstructs a **full brain in pure Rust** (192×256×256 in ~4 min at ~10 GB), no ONNX Runtime dependency.

## Details

- Feature-gated: `onnx` (tract, WASM-capable) and `download` (ureq + sha2). Default build unaffected.
- Registry is pure data; WASM hosts read its URLs to fetch weights in JS.
- Tests in `tests/models_onnx.rs` (ignored by default; point at local ONNX via env vars).

title: feat(separation): add DECOMPOSE and HC-ChiSep χ-separation
body:
Adds two more classical (no deep-learning) susceptibility-source-separation methods ported from QSM-CI, closing the remaining non-DL chi-separation gaps against the QSM-CI algorithm set.

## Methods

### `decompose` — DECOMPOSE (Chen et al. 2021, NeuroImage)
Signal-domain separation: a 3-compartment (paramagnetic / diamagnetic / neutral) complex multi-echo GRE signal is fit per voxel with a 3-stage alternating bounded least-squares, exactly as the reference. Like the QSM-CI submission, the phase is synthesized from the provided χ_total so this isolates the separation step.

- Adds a small **bounded Levenberg–Marquardt** solver (finite-diff Jacobian, box projection) for the 1–3 parameter fit stages — the repo had no generic bounded NLS.
- Embarrassingly parallel per voxel (`maybe_par_iter!`); ~130 s over 1.31 M brain voxels on 14 cores.
- **Output-mapping note:** uses the physically-consistent mapping χ+ = |PSC| (paramagnetic sub-model), χ− = −|DSC|. The QSM-CI reference *comment* claims the opposite swap (χ+ = |DSC|); that anti-correlates with the qsm-forward ground truth, so it is deliberately **not** replicated (see module docs).

### `hc_chisep` — Hollow-Cylinder χ-separation (Wharton & Bowtell model)
Derives white-matter fibre orientation from the multi-echo magnitude's multi-compartment interference (no DTI), then separates via an R2'-anchored (θ, MWF) grid search + closed-form non-WM branch, blended by a soft WM-likeness weight.

- **Headline mode only** — the reference's env-gated optional regularisers (TV/guided joint inversion, R2' denoise, hard constraint) are off by default and omitted.
- Adds scipy-matching `gaussian_filter` / `median_filter` (reflect boundary) helpers.
- Optional spin-echo magnitude used as soft MWF evidence when present.

## Results (qsm-forward chisep phantom, 7 T)

| Method | χ+ corr | χ− corr | χ+ xsim | χ− xsim | runtime |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| DECOMPOSE | 0.577 | 0.793 | 0.339 | 0.415 | ~133 s |
| HC-ChiSep | 0.937 | 0.914 | 0.806 | 0.862 | ~12 s |

HC-ChiSep is on par with the flagship `chi_sep_ilsqr`. DECOMPOSE is a coarser per-voxel signal-domain separator (no R2'), as expected for the method. Output maps are anatomically correct (χ+ bright in deep gray-matter iron; χ− bright in white-matter myelin).

## Conventions & wiring
- ppm in/out, `(chi_pos ≥ 0, chi_neg ≤ 0, chi_total = χ+ + χ−)` return, `impl FnMut(usize,usize)` progress, `#[cfg_attr(feature = "introspection", ...)]` on params — matching `wavesep` / `r2star_qsm`.
- Multi-echo magnitude uses the voxel-major `(n_voxels, n_echoes)` layout (same as `r2star_qsm_from_magnitude`).
- Unit tests in each module (run in normal CI); `#[ignore]` phantom integration tests added to `tests/chisep_relaxometry_qsmci.rs`.
- **CI (`chisep-demo`)** updated so the automated PR comment renders figures + metrics for both new methods (`render_slices.py` NAMES/WINDOWS + workflow figure sections). The workflow already runs the whole `chisep_relaxometry_qsmci` binary, so both are picked up automatically.

Builds and unit tests pass in both serial and `--features parallel` modes.

title: Add mSMV, R2*-QSM and WaveSep (ported from QSM-CI)
body:
Three classical (non-deep-learning) QSM methods from the [QSM-CI](https://github.com/QSMxT/QSM-CI) platform that QSM.rs was missing — all pure-Rust, no trained weights.

## New algorithms

| Method | Stage | Module | Reference |
|---|---|---|---|
| **mSMV** | background field removal | `bgremove::msmv` | Roberts et al., MRM 2024 |
| **R2\*-QSM** | χ-separation | `separation::r2star_qsm` | Dimov et al., Tomography/JNI 2022 |
| **WaveSep** | χ-separation | `separation::wavesep` | Fang et al., MLCN/MICCAI 2023 |

- **mSMV** — maximum spherical mean value BFR: SMV prefilter + boundary shadow correction, preserving the brain edge (no erosion). Takes the field in ppm, converts ppm↔rad internally for the radian shadow threshold `0.01·B0/3` (which the binary SMV kernel reaches analytically, so the upstream fine kernel sweep is skipped).
- **R2\*-QSM** — closed-form paramagnetic/diamagnetic separation from a QSM (χ_total) + R2\*, **no R2′ needed**. `r2star_qsm_from_magnitude` additionally fits R2\* by magnitude-weighted log-linear (matching the QSM-CI reference).
- **WaveSep** — ISTA proximal-gradient with two data fidelities (χ₊+χ₋≈χ_total, χ₊−χ₋≈R2′/Dr) plus a wavelet-L1 prior. Extends `utils/wavelet.rs` to **db3/db4** with a pywt-matching `dwt_max_level`.

## Conventions

Separation methods follow the existing `chi_sep_ilsqr`/`chi_sep_medi` convention: return `(chi_pos, chi_neg ≤ 0, chi_total)` in ppm. Iterative methods (WaveSep, mSMV) take a `progress` callback, matching the rest of the library.

## Results (QSM-CI chisep phantom, 164×205×205, 7T)

| Method | χ+ corr | χ− corr | runtime |
|---|---|---|---|
| R2\*-QSM | 0.935 | 0.863 | 63 ms |
| WaveSep | 0.943 | 0.814 | 13.7 s |

Competitive with the leaderboard classical χ-separation entries.

## Tests & CI

- Unit tests for all three modules; env-gated phantom integration tests (`tests/chisep_relaxometry_qsmci.rs`, `test_bgremove_msmv`).
- **mSMV** wired into `integration-tests.yml` (BFR detect matrix + PR-comment table).
- **R2\*-QSM / WaveSep** wired into `chisep-demo.yml` (metrics table + figures).
- 560 lib unit tests pass; clippy clean on new code.

## Notes

- The mSMV BFR quality gates (`corr > 0.6`, `nrmse < 0.6`) are conservative floors set without running against the OSF `bids/` data locally (mSMV keeps brain-edge voxels where the reference local field is least reliable). Can be tightened once run in CI.
- Unrelated AMP-PE pipeline-dispatcher changes that were present in the working tree were intentionally **left out** of this branch.

title: perf(inversion): parallelize AMP-PE (~2x on multi-core)
body:
## Summary

AMP-PE was single-threaded except for the FFT (~13% of runtime). Profiling at the real bids scale (168×208×208) showed the rest — **parameter estimation (~50%)**, **wavelet transform (~23%)**, and the O(N) elementwise passes (~12%) — running serially even with `--features parallel`. This PR parallelizes them and trims allocations, for **~2.1× end-to-end** on a 14-core machine, with numerically-unchanged output.

The WASM / no-`parallel` path is preserved (serial fallback), and results are **bit-identical between the serial and parallel builds** (thread-count and feature-flag independent).

## Changes

- **GAMP parameter estimation** (`input_parameter_est`, `mix_output_parameter_est`, `mix_output_function`) → **deterministic chunked reductions**: each fixed-size chunk sums sequentially and chunks combine in index order, so the sum is independent of thread count. Adds a `maybe_par_chunks!` macro next to the existing `maybe_par_*` ones.
- **Wavelet transform** (`utils/wavelet.rs`): parallelize each 1D-along-axis pass over its independent *lines* — distinct lines write disjoint strided output indices, so per-line raw-pointer writes are race-free (same pattern as the `SendPtr` in `fft.rs`). Also split the inner tap loop into an interior (direct-index) part and a low-boundary (wraparound) part, dropping a `rem_euclid` division per tap.
- **Elementwise GAMP passes** → `maybe_par_iter` (exact, elementwise). Reuse the adjoint scatter buffer (non-mask positions stay zero ⇒ no per-call clear), fuse the `mut_cst` scaling into the adjoint output, and hoist the invariant AWGN `mse` out of the inner sweep.

## Verification

Re-verified against the MATLAB reference and a pre-optimization baseline (synthetic db2/nlevel3/12+12 and the real 164×205×205 phantom):

| check | result |
|---|---|
| synthetic vs MATLAB | nrmse **6.567e-7** (unchanged) |
| bids 8+8 vs MATLAB (double seed) | nrmse **2.193e-10** (unchanged) |
| vs pre-optimization baseline | nrmse **5.7e-16** (chunked-reduction rounding only) |
| serial vs parallel build | **bit-identical** |

Timing (bids 8+8, same 14-core box under identical load, min of 4):

| build | time |
|---|---|
| baseline (`main`) | 153.4 s |
| this PR | **73.7 s** (~2.1×) |

Full library suite passes (550 tests) on both feature configs; no new clippy warnings.

title: feat(inversion): add AMP-PE nonlinear dipole inversion
body:
## Summary

Adds **AMP-PE** (Approximate Message Passing with Parameter Estimation; Huang et al., *MRM* 2023 — [EmoryCN2L/QSM_AMP_PE](https://github.com/EmoryCN2L/QSM_AMP_PE)) as a new dipole-inversion algorithm: GAMP over a linearized wrapped-phase forward model with a Laplace sparse-wavelet prior and a two-stage (single-Gaussian → Gaussian-mixture) noise model.

Public API mirrors the other inversions:
```rust
let chi = inversion::amp_pe(&local_field_ppm, &mask, magnitude.as_deref(), &grid, bdir, &AmpPeParams::default(), |_, _| {});
```

## New modules
- **`inversion/amp_pe.rs`** — `amp_pe` / `AmpPeParams`, the two-stage GAMP solver + linearization driver. Reuses the existing dipole kernel and `Fft3dWorkspace`; the weighted-dipole operator's Frobenius norm has an exact closed form, so it's computed deterministically rather than probe-estimated (a strict improvement over the reference's 2-random-probe estimate).
- **`utils/wavelet.rs`** — periodic 3D Daubechies db1/db2 transform (a `wavedec3`/`waverec3` equivalent in `'per'` mode). Orthonormal, so synthesis is the exact adjoint of analysis (perfect reconstruction).
- **`utils/special.rs`** — `erf`/`erfc`/`erfcx` via Cody's SPECFUN (the same routine MATLAB uses); `erfcx` is needed by the GAMP parameter estimation.

## Verification against the original MATLAB
Driven by the actual vendored solver with deterministic (injected) operator norms:

| case | Rust vs MATLAB |
|---|---|
| synthetic, db1/db2 × nlevel 2/3 × ±magnitude, 5–12 iters | nrmse ~1e-6, corr 1.0 |
| **real 164×205×205 phantom, 8+8 iters (double seed)** | **nrmse 2.2e-10** |

Component-level: wavelet matches `wavedec3` to 4e-12, `erfcx` to 1e-13, dipole forward to 1e-16, chiL2 seed to 2e-7.

Two findings worth noting:
- The chiL2 seed must be computed on the field **masked to the ROI** (as `recon.m` does) — otherwise background outside the mask leaks in. Only shows on real data; guarded by the `amp_pe_ignores_out_of_mask_field` regression test.
- The reference's `dipole_kernel_angulated` computes its seed in **single precision**. In phase-wrapping regions (|phase|>π — real data reaches ~5.2 rad; synthetic stays <0.2), the nonlinear AMP is multistable, so that ~1e-7 quirk can flip a localized region to a different local solution. This crate uses full double precision (MATLAB-with-double-seed agrees to 2e-10).

## Tests
- Unit tests: `special::` (erf/erfc/erfcx vs MATLAB values), `wavelet::` (perfect reconstruction + orthonormality, db1/db2, non-cubic), `amp_pe::` (masking, finiteness, out-of-mask invariance).
- `tests/amppe_qsmci.rs` — `#[ignore]` end-to-end quality gate on the qsm-forward phantom (masked corr ≈ 0.79 vs ground truth at 8+8 iters, no magnitude weighting). Run with `AMPPE_BIDS=<path> cargo test --release --test amppe_qsmci -- --ignored`.

Full library suite passes (545 tests); no new clippy warnings in the added files.

title: refactor(separation): ppm field input convention + perf groundwork
body:
Follow-up to #59 (the first two commits were pushed to the branch just after the merge; the third adds FFT padding).

## ppm input alignment
`chi_sep_ilsqr` and `chi_sep_medi` now take the local field in **ppm** like the dipole-inversion algorithms (cf. the TFI ppm fix), converting to Hz internally via `params.cf` — previously callers converted ppm→Hz with the same `cf` they also passed in params. Test gamma aligned to the library-wide 42.576 MHz/T. Phantom validation unchanged: χ+ 0.953 corr / 0.781 xsim, χ− 0.873 / 0.667.

## Perf: parallel TV stencils + zero hot-loop allocations
`fgrad`/`bdiv` now run one rayon task per z-slab (same pattern as the TGV stencils — MEDI benefits too), and both chi-sep CG operators reuse preallocated scratch instead of cloning ~28 MB buffers per iteration. **No measurable end-to-end speedup** on the qsmci phantom (interleaved A/B within noise) — the `perf_probe` micro-benchmark shows the already-parallel FFTs are ~90% of the CG operator at 164×205×205 (both dims contain the prime 41). Kept because the changes are strictly better and bit-identical.

## Transparent FFT-size padding
Generic `pad3d`/`unpad3d` added to the padding utils (which had `next_fast_fft_size` all along, unused by any algorithm). Both chi-sep functions now zero-pad non-2/3/5-smooth volumes to the next fast size internally and crop outputs back — callers see original-size volumes throughout. Probe: one dipole apply drops 278 ms → 139 ms (2× despite +22% voxels). End-to-end: 156.7 s → 145.7 s mean (~7%, within machine noise) since the padded volume makes non-FFT work proportionally more expensive. Accuracy-neutral (χ+ xsim 0.7807 → 0.7803), standard QSM practice, and protects against pathological (e.g. prime) acquisition dims.

Natural follow-up: apply the same padding wrapper to the other FFT-heavy algorithms (iLSQR, TKD, V-SHARP, …).

title: feat(separation): chi-separation (Shin 2021) validated against QSM-CI
body:
Adds the original χ-separation algorithm (Shin et al. 2021, NeuroImage 240:118371) as `chi_sep_ilsqr`, validated on the QSM-CI chi-separation phantom with the QSM-CI metrics.

## Algorithm
Paper-based port of the SNU-LIST toolbox's `chi_sep_iLSQR` (the toolbox ships it compiled; the cost function comes from the paper's Supplementary Methods):
- Complex data term `‖Wr·(R2′ − Dr₊|χ+| − Dr₋|χ−|) + i·2π·Wf·(f − D∗(χ++χ−))‖²` — the real (R2′) and imaginary (field) parts decouple into two SNR-weighted least-squares terms with a physics-fixed 2π coupling
- `Wr = Wf/10` where R2′ is unreliable (>30 Hz or <1 Hz)
- Edge-masked L1 TV: `2λ1` on χ_total (magnitude edge mask) + `λ1` per component (R2′ edge mask), IRLS-linearized
- Voxelwise 2×2 initialization from a conventional QSM (our iLSQR on the same local field — feeding an external χ_total is known to break the method, per the QSM-CI diagnostic)
- Projected Gauss-Newton/CG with sign constraints (χ+ ≥ 0, χ− ≤ 0), ≤30 iterations

## Validation (QSM-CI chisep phantom, 7T, QSM-CI metrics)

| method | χ+ corr / xsim | χ− corr / xsim | runtime |
|---|---|---|---|
| **QSM.rs chi_sep_ilsqr** | **0.953 / 0.781** | **0.873 / 0.667** | ~4 min |
| MATLAB chi-sep-ilsqr (posted) | 0.862 / 0.590 | 0.807 / 0.480 | 30 min |
| MATLAB chi-sep-medi (posted) | 0.904 / 0.731 | 0.911 / 0.580 | 3 min |
| χ-sepnet, DL (posted) | 0.944 / 0.887 | 0.884 / 0.719 | 1 min |

Posted numbers are from a slightly older phantom generation (GT corr 0.935 between versions), so they're a baseline zone rather than an exact head-to-head.

## CI

title: feat(relaxometry): B1-map input for r2_epg + ~2.5x faster Gibbs unringing
body:
Two follow-ups from the relaxometry session (STATUS.md §5):

## Optional per-voxel B1-map input for `r2_epg`
When a B1 map is supplied (e.g. from a separate B1 acquisition), each voxel's B1 snaps to the nearest `b1_grid` entry and only that dictionary column is searched — a T2-only fit. This keeps EPG's stimulated-echo bias correction while removing the free B1 parameter that overfits noise at low SNR (STATUS §4, lesson 4). New unit tests cover R2 recovery with a correct fixed B1, off-grid snapping, and that a wrong fixed B1 actually constrains (biases) the fit.

## Gibbs unringing ~2.5× faster (128³: 1.35 s → 0.54 s)
Not via the previously-deferred approximate-upsampling idea (FLOP analysis: a 50× zero-padded IFFT costs about the same as the 90 small IFFTs it replaces). Instead:
1. **Paired-shift IFFTs** — with the even-n Nyquist bin symmetrised, the ± shifted spectra are each Hermitian, so `IFFT(c·(ph + i·conj(ph)))` yields both real shifted lines in one transform (halves FFT work, removes the per-sample `sqrt`).
2. **Mod-free TV** — `tv_min_line` stages neighbour differences in a scratch array; the interior sliding sums need no `%`.

Output vs old implementation (128³ synthetic phantom): corr 0.999999995, mean |diff| 1.3e-5, max |diff| 3.9e-3 (unit-scale) — the deviation is confined to the even-length Nyquist bin and is documented in the module doc. The DIPY faithful-port reference test passes unchanged. An ignored `bench_unring_volume` test is added as a repeatable perf baseline.

All 537 unit tests pass; no new clippy warnings.

title: feat(utils): exact anisotropic Euclidean distance transform
body:
## What

Adds an exact, anisotropic **Euclidean distance transform** for binary masks in `src/utils/distance.rs` — the separable O(n) algorithm of Felzenszwalb & Huttenlocher (2012), generalized to non-unit voxel spacing. For each foreground voxel it returns the distance in **mm** to the nearest background voxel.

## Why

On high-resolution / sub-100µm data, SMV and morphological erosion radii specified in **mm** can exceed the object's thickness and silently erode a mask to (almost) nothing — which is exactly what happens to VSHARP on 16.4T 0.03mm specimen data (default 1.0mm min radius vs a mask only 0.99mm thick → empty local field → empty QSM). This EDT lets callers *predict and prevent* that before running a pipeline, and auto-suggest voxel-appropriate radii. It's a general primitive reusable across QSM.rs consumers (qsmxt.rs, qsmbly).

## API

- `distance_transform_edt(mask, grid) -> Vec<f64>` — EDT in mm
- `mask_max_thickness(mask, grid) -> f64` — deepest interior distance (largest kernel radius that leaves anything)
- `erosion_survivors(mask, grid, radius_mm) -> usize` — voxels surviving a spherical kernel of radius r
- `suggest_radius_for_fraction(mask, grid, keep_fraction) -> f64` — largest radius retaining a target fraction

## Tests / validation

- 6 unit tests (1-D, anisotropic spacing, 3-D corner, all-background, erosion monotonicity, radius suggestion).
- Validated on a real 13.1M-voxel 0.03mm mask: runs in ~0.5s, reports max thickness 0.99mm, predicts 0 survivors at the 1.0mm default radius (matching the observed collapse).

Purely additive — only `src/utils/distance.rs` (new) and the `utils` module re-exports.

title: feat(relaxometry): EPG R2/R2', MP-PCA denoising, Gibbs unringing
body:
Adds a relaxometry toolkit to QSM.rs for deriving **R2′ = R2\* − R2** — the input chi-separation (`chi_sep_medi`) needs — from multi-echo GRE (R2\*) + multi-echo spin-echo / MESE (R2), plus two complementary preprocessing tools. All standalone, opt-in library functions.

## What's added
- **`qsm_core::relaxometry`** — `epg_cpmg_echoes` (CPMG EPG forward model, Weigel 2015), `r2_epg` (per-voxel R2 from MESE via EPG dictionary matching over a T2×B1 grid; returns R2 in Hz + refocusing B1), `r2prime`. EPG corrects the stimulated-echo bias a mono-exponential fit suffers under imperfect refocusing (B1 < 1).
- **`qsm_core::denoise`** — `mppca_denoise`: Marchenko–Pastur PCA denoising (Veraart 2016 / DIPY port) with a hand-written Jacobi eigensolver (no linalg dep). Removes random noise along the echo dim, edge-preserving.
- **`qsm_core::unring`** — `gibbs_unring{,_volume,_masked}`: Kellner-2016 subvoxel-shift unringing, generalised from DIPY's 2D-slice form to full 3D; allocation-free, parallel; masked variant unrings only a bounding box.
- **Fix** — `r2star_arlo` was a biased ratio-mean (an `alpha ≤ 1` filter kept only downward noise fluctuations, inflating R2\*); replaced with the genuine Pei-2015 integral ARLO. R2\* correlation 0.20 → 0.62 on a 16-echo phantom; also improves the pipeline R2\*/T2\* maps.

## Testing & CI
- Unit tests: EPG↔mono-exp equivalence, MP-PCA/Jacobi numerics, Gibbs port-fidelity vs DIPY (<5e-3). These run in the existing unit-tests workflow.
- **New `Relaxometry Demo` workflow** builds a small **synthetic** phantom in-code (no external data), asserts each tool works (EPG less biased than mono-exp, R2′ recovers truth, MP-PCA improves noisy R2\*, unringing reduces ringing), and posts a **PR comment with a metrics table + before/after figures**. See the comment this PR will generate.

## Notes
- The R2′-subtraction is noise-sensitive by nature (small difference of two larger rates); MP-PCA helps at low SNR and Gibbs unringing removes truncation ringing — both are opt-in preprocessing. `STATUS.md` documents the fuller investigation and lessons.
- Wiring these into the QSMxT pipeline (MESE discovery + MESE→GRE reslice + R2′/chi-sep stages) is follow-up work, not in this PR.

title: fix(tfi): take the field in ppm (like NDI), not radians
body:
TFI inherited MEDI's radians convention (ppm→rad in, rad→ppm out). MEDI gets the *small* local field so ×~6.4 stays sub-π; TFI gets the *large total field*, so scaling to radians wraps it in the `exp(i·field)` data term and wrecks the result (**corr ~0.16** via the pipeline/CLI vs **~0.70** when fed ppm).

**NDI is also a nonlinear `exp()` method yet takes ppm directly** — that's the correct precedent. This makes TFI take the field in **ppm** (no conversion), consistent with NDI and the majority of inversions; χ returns in ppm.

- `pipeline/inversion.rs`: Tfi arm feeds `local_field_ppm` directly (drops the rad round-trip).
- `tfi()` docs: input is ppm; don't pre-scale to radians.
- `test_tfi_phantom` (#[ignore]): fed ppm to match.

The `tfi()` solver itself is unchanged — it already worked with ppm (the integration test feeds ppm and scores ~0.70). All lib + pipeline tests pass.

title: Add TFI (preconditioned total field inversion)
body:
Adds **TFI** (preconditioned Total Field Inversion; Z. Liu et al., *Magn Reson Med* 2017, [doi:10.1002/mrm.26946](https://doi.org/10.1002/mrm.26946)) as a new single-step dipole-inversion method.

TFI inverts the **total field** (before background removal) directly to susceptibility over the whole FOV, jointly handling background removal and dipole inversion. Built on the existing MEDI nonlinear Gauss-Newton + CG + L1-morphology machinery, with:
- a **preconditioner** change-of-variables χ = P⊙y (P = 1 in the brain mask, `precond` outside),
- whole-FOV L1 regularization (morphology edges in-brain, smoothing out-of-brain),
- an SNR data weight (~0 out-of-brain).

The CG operator wraps MEDI's: `A_tfi(δy) = P⊙A_medi(P⊙δy)`, `b_tfi = P⊙b_medi`.

## Changes
- New `src/inversion/tfi.rs` — `tfi()`, `TfiParams`, `cg_solve_tfi`, unit tests, and an `#[ignore]`d phantom validation.
- `medi.rs` — expose reused helpers as `pub(crate)` (visibility only; MEDI numerics + all its tests unchanged).
- `InversionAlgorithm::Tfi` wired into config + pipeline dispatch (ppm↔rad conversion like MEDI).

## Validation
In-silico dev phantom (total field → χ, within mask): **correlation 0.995**, detrended NRMSE 10.3. All 521 lib tests pass; 14/14 MEDI tests unchanged.

| Method | corr | XSIM | NRMSE% |
|---|---|---|---|
| FANSI nlTGV | **0.947** | 0.690 | 33% |
| NDI | 0.879 | 0.616 | 48% |
| L1-QSM | 0.869 | 0.563 | 50% |

title: test(ilsqr): add standalone iLSQR dipole-inversion integration test

## Why

iLSQR had **no direct integration test** — it was only exercised indirectly through `test_pipeline_qsmart`. QSMART wraps iLSQR in SDF background removal + vasculature/curvature weighting and runs it **twice**, so the pipeline metric is a muddy readout of the inversion itself. That's precisely why the Step‑1 LSQR premature-convergence bug (fixed in #48) went unnoticed for so long, and why #48's QSMART CI delta was ambiguous (XSIM ↑, NRMSE slightly ↓).

## What

- **`test_inversion_ilsqr`** in `tests/integration_tests.rs`, mirroring the other 7 inversion tests: runs `inversion::ilsqr` on the clean local field with default params, scores χ against ground truth, and asserts `nrmse < 0.5` / `correlation > 0.7` — the same bounds every other inversion method (incl. the cruder TKD/TSVD) clears on this data.

title: fix(ilsqr): use relative-residual LSQR stop (match kamesy Step 1)
body:
## Problem

iLSQR was under-performing because its **Step-1 weighted LSQR** (`lsqr_complex` in `src/inversion/ilsqr.rs`) stopped too early. It used the augmented Paige–Saunders test from `lsqrSOL`:

```
||r||/||b|| <= btol + atol*||A||*||x||/||b||
```

The `atol*||A||*||x||/||b||` term inflates the threshold, so Step 1 stopped at **~iteration 10 (relres ≈ 0.09)** and fed a badly under-converged `xlsqr` straight into the final susceptibility map.

The kamesy reference this port follows (`QSM.m` `src/inversion/ilsqr.m`, Step 1 `lsqr_`) calls MATLAB's **built-in** `lsqr(afun, b, tol, maxit)`, which stops purely on the relative residual `||b - A*x||/||b|| <= tol` (~39 iterations on the dev volume).

## Fix

Switch `lsqr_complex` to the simple relative-residual stop (`test1 <= atol`). `lsqr_complex` is used **only by iLSQR**, so no other inversion method changes.

## Result

Per-stage agreement vs the kamesy MATLAB reference (dev volume, masked):

| Stage | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `xlsqr` (Step 1) | corr 0.982 / NRMSE 19.1% | **corr 1.0000 / 0.43%** |
| final `chi` | corr 0.983 / NRMSE 19.0% | **corr 1.0000 / 0.32%** |

Local `qsm-eval` score: **NRMSE 32.7% → 26.3%, XSIM 0.179 → 0.213**, landing exactly on the kamesy reference.

Note: this closes the QSM.rs-vs-kamesy **port** gap. A remaining gap to STI Suite's iLSQR is **algorithmic** (kamesy vs STI), not a port bug.

## Tests

All 10 iLSQR tests pass, plus a new regression test `test_lsqr_complex_relres_stop` (ill-conditioned diagonal) that fails under the old augmented test and passes with the relative-residual stop.

title: tgv: default to Langkammer reference regularization (fix over-smoothing)
body:
## Problem
`TgvParams::default()` uses `alpha1 = alpha0 = 0.001`. `alpha1` (the first-order/gradient TGV weight) at 0.001 is ~2× the classic Langkammer TGV-QSM reference and **over-smooths** the susceptibility map.

Measured on a simulated 7T volume (in-mask, vs ground-truth χ; GT mean|∇| = 0.01560):

| alpha1 / alpha0 | xsim | nrmse | mean\|∇\| |
|---|---|---|---|
| **0.001 / 0.001 (current default)** | 0.325 | 64.8% | 0.00739 (47% of GT) |
| **0.0005 / 0.0015 (Langkammer — this PR)** | **0.468** | **56.2%** | 0.00939 |
| 0.0003 / 0.001 (single-volume optimum) | 0.503 | 55.4% | 0.01117 |

I chose the **citation-backed Langkammer value** rather than the single-volume optimum (0.0003) to avoid overfitting the library default to one synthetic phantom — Langkammer is validated across real datasets and still resolves the over-smoothing.

## Scope
- Only `TgvParams::default()` changes. **QSMxT inherits this automatically** (`args.alpha1.unwrap_or(d.alpha1)`), so its `invert tgv` default improves with no QSMxT change.
- `get_default_alpha(level)` (test-only; "level 2" = 0.001/0.001) is **left as-is** and now differs from the struct default — flagging for you to reconcile the level table separately if desired.

title: bgremove: absolute-mm radii + defaults that match what CI validates
body:
## Problem

The SMV-based background-removal methods exposed their kernel radius as a `*_factor` of voxel size, and their `Default` impls had **drifted away from the values the integration tests actually validate**:

| Method | `Default` (what qsmxt / QSM-CI / pipeline get) | CI test hardcoded (validated) |
|---|---|---|
| SHARP | `radius_factor: 18.0` → **~18 mm** | `6.0 / min_voxel` → **6 mm** |
| V-SHARP | threshold `0.001`, max `18`, min `2` | threshold `0.05`, max **12 mm**, min **1 mm** |
| iSMV | radius `2.0`, tol `1e-3`, iter `500` | radius **5 mm**, tol `1e-6`, iter `50` |

An 18 mm SHARP kernel erodes **~90%** of the brain (empirically: 6.7% of voxels survive on an 80³ sphere vs ~52% at 6 mm). So every consumer that used the defaults — qsmxt, QSM-CI, the pipeline — got a result that **no test ever exercised**, and the QSM-CI leaderboard showed SHARP far worse than the QSM.rs PR-CI image. The `18.0` was introduced in the #42 Params-struct refactor while the CI was simultaneously changed to hardcode `6.0 / min_voxel`; the default and the validated value silently diverged.

## Fix (update the defaults; make the tests use them — no hardcoding)

- **Radii are now absolute mm** (consistent with `ResharpParams.radius`), dropping the voxel coupling and the `6.0 / vsx` hack:
  - `SharpParams { threshold, radius }` — default **6.0 mm**
  - `VsharpParams { threshold, max_radius, min_radius }` — defaults **12.0 / 1.0 mm**, threshold **0.05**
  - `IsmvParams { tol, max_iter, radius }` — default **5.0 mm**, tol 1e-6, max_iter 50
- **`integration_tests.rs` now builds these via `::default()`**, so the tests validate exactly what users get and future drift fails CI. The new defaults **equal the old hardcoded values**, so results and assertions are unchanged — only the *source* of the numbers moved into `Default`.
- **`TestResult` now also reports the challenge NRMSE** (demeaned `100·‖r−t‖/‖t‖`, the same metric QSM-CI shows), and the CI background-removal table gains an `NRMSE% (χ)` column — so this repo's PR CI and the QSM-CI leaderboard report the same headline number (the existing range-normalized NRMSE stays too).

## ⚠️ Breaking API change

`SharpParams.radius_factor → radius` (mm); `VsharpParams.max_radius_factor/min_radius_factor → max_radius/min_radius` (mm); `IsmvParams.radius_factor → radius` (mm).

**Downstream follow-up (separate repo):** the `qsmxt` CLI (`qsmxt.rs`) references these fields and exposes `--radius-factor`; it needs a matching PR (rename `--radius-factor → --radius`, pass mm) and an image rebuild before QSM-CI picks up the new defaults.

## Verification
- `cargo build --tests` clean; `cargo test --lib bgremove` → 51 passed.
- Integration tests unchanged in effective params → expected green; please eyeball the CI background-removal images/table (SHARP now reflects the **default** 6 mm).

## Not in this PR (noted for later)
Other tests still hardcode params that differ from their defaults (e.g. TKD `0.2` vs default `0.15`, RESHARP `max_iter` 200 vs 30). Left alone to keep this focused on the SMV/erosion regression; can follow up.

title: perf: parallelise the QSM pipeline (single-subject multicore)
body:
## Motivation

Within a single subject the pipeline was effectively single-core: only the free-function FFT path (V-SHARP/PDF) parallelised, while the iterative inversions, phase unwrapping, masking, and TGV ran serially regardless of thread count. A 5-echo scanner run pinned one core the whole time.

This PR parallelises the serial hot paths, all gated behind the existing `parallel` feature so **WASM/qsmbly is unaffected** (feature off → plain iterators, no rayon linked). Every change is per-voxel/per-echo deterministic, so outputs are **bit-identical** and covered by existing tests.

## Commits

- **`fft`** — give `Fft3dWorkspace::fft3d/ifft3d` a rayon path (shared `transform_3d_par`, per-thread scratch). The workspace was always sequential, so **RTS, iLSQR, MEDI, TV, NLTV** (which reuse the plan workspace) got no thread benefit. Free `fft3d()` now delegates to the workspace; duplicated `fft3d_parallel/ifft3d_parallel` removed.
- **`romeo` (echo)** — fan out the per-echo loop in `unwrap_individual` (the qsmxt default `individual=true`). Independent region-grows now run concurrently.
- **`romeo` (masking/weights)** — parallelise `calculate_weights_romeo_with_flags` and `voxel_quality_romeo`. These feed both the phase-quality masking **and** the ROMEO unwrap weights, so both stages speed up.
- **`tgv`** — parallelise the per-iteration f32 finite-difference stencils across z-slabs (`apply_stencil`, `apply_laplacian`, and `fgrad/symgrad/symdiv/bdiv_masked` in `gradient.rs`, which are shared with TV/NLTV). TGV uses no FFT, so it was previously fully serial.

## Measured (14 threads)

End-to-end on a 164×205×205, 4-echo, RTS/ROMEO/V-SHARP run:

| | Total | avg cores |
|---|---:|---:|
| before | 28.3s | 1.47 |
| after | **13.7s** | **3.33** |

Per-stage: RTS 9.3→4.0s, unwrap 7.6→2.8s, mask 4.2→0.7s. TGV component bench (128³, 200 iters): 11.0→6.8s (1.63×).

FFT parallelism is memory-bandwidth-bound (sub-linear); the remaining serial cores are inherently-sequential region-growing and the not-yet-parallelised TGV element-wise update loops.

## Validation

- Builds with and without `parallel`; the previously-trivial `test_{fft,ifft}3d_workspace_parallel_matches_sequential` now actually exercise the parallel path.
- fft / inversion / romeo / masking / field_mapping / gradient / tgv unit tests pass, plus the RTS and ROMEO-B0 integration tests on the forward-sim phantom.

title: Use relative tolerance in LBV for unit-independent convergence
body:
## Summary
